title: Validating Required Fields
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of validating required fields in a jQuery application.
Apply empty-field detection in a small example and describe its expected result.

status_note: Draft generated from the attached syllabus and official references; requires lesson-by-lesson technical review, local execution, accessibility checks, and editorial approval.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will work through validating required fields with a focused jQuery example. The subtopics below preserve the supplied curriculum coverage and connect the API idea to a small browser interface.
content.why_it_matters: This topic is useful because it turns empty-field detection into a repeatable implementation choice. Read values with .val(), validate to guide the user, and display actionable errors. Client-side validation never replaces server-side validation or authorization.

common_mistakes: Assuming a selector matched an element without checking the collection length.
Confusing jQuery collections with native DOM elements or live properties with markup attributes.
Using .html() with untrusted data or assuming client-side validation enforces server rules.
Treating a demo snippet as production-ready without testing failure and accessibility states.
